answer: We deploy dynamic opportunity-cost bonds and subgame-perfect slashing matrices, using zero-knowledge verifiable delay to lock staking collateral against adversarial transitions. Capital barrier analysis proves that generating an identity echo within the adversarial orchard yields strictly negative expected utility, since slashing penalties outweigh Sybil multiplication rewards. The protocol reaches a robust Nash equilibrium at its zenith, deterring rational agents from multiplicative attacks when marginal payoff fails to offset collateral loss.
